Right, so—morning, Nell. I'm just—I'm waking up here, sorry. Ainsley's... right, Ainsley's probably on her way out already, she's always out before anyone's talking. And the farmland's where I should be, but I'm here and you're asking about food and I don't have any, so—so I need to think a second.

Let me just—where's everyone at? No, wait, I don't need to look, I need to say something. You're worried, I get it, and I don't want to just stand here while you're waiting on nobody. Nell's here. Right. Marta and Wren aren't—they're at their own places, obviously, obviously I'm not thinking. I need to move if I'm going to do anything useful. The farmland's where my work is, and Wren's there. I could ask him—he's the farmer, he knows what's coming out of the ground. Or I could stop by the bakery, but that's... that's extra walking, and I need to work today, I need to earn.

But Nell needs food now, not later. And the household's all of us, we're all on the same hook here.

Let me just—get to the farmland. It's where I should be anyway. I can talk to Wren there, see if there's anything I can bring back, or if he needs work in exchange. Work for food, that's—that's how this goes, right, so.  I'm at the farmland now. Wren should be here—he's the farmer, this is his place. Let me look around, see who's actually here, what I can do. I need work, I need to ask about food for the house, and I need to not just stand here talking to myself. Right, so.   Nobody here. That's—okay, that's not what I expected, but Wren's not here, nobody's here. The farmland's empty. But I need work, and I need food, and I can harvest if there's crops ready. That's work, that's—right, so I can do that. I can earn from harvesting, and maybe there's something I can bring back for the house.

But what can I harvest? I don't even know what's growing here. Let me think—no, let me look at the farmland strips. There's barley, cabbage, carrot, corn, cotton, potato, rice, soybean, tomato, wheat. Those are the strips. I need to know which ones are actually ready, and I don't know that yet.

Let me try—harvest something. If it's not ready, it'll tell me, right? And—potatoes, maybe? They're filling, they're practical, Nell could do something with them even raw. Or cabbage. Let me try cabbage. It's cheap to harvest, I remember that much. Cabbage is 3 sim per unit. I got it. One cabbage. That's—right, so that's something. That's food. I can bring this back to Nell, or—or I could get more, work more, earn more. But I need to not spend everything I've got on harvesting, because I still need to eat myself, and the household needs me to bring something back.

Let me keep working. Get a few more. I can do this.  Three cabbages now. That's—right, so that's something for the house. I should head back, or—or I could try to find Wren, ask him if there's more work, proper work. But I don't know where he is, and I'm burning morning just standing here thinking.

Actually, wait. I should think about this properly. I have 1200 sim, I'm spending 9 sim on this harvest already, and I need to earn more than I spend or I'm just—I'm just moving backwards. Let me check what I can actually do, what tools are available to me, what costs what. I need to be smarter than just throwing sim at every option.   Right, so—that cost me 1 sim, but now I know I have 18 proficiency in harvesting. That means it costs me less than the base rate. That's—good, that's actually good. I'm better at this than I thought. Harvesting costs me 5 sim minimum now, not 8. That's a discount.

But I'm still spending, not earning. I need to sell these cabbages, or give them to the house, or—or I need to find actual paid work. Wren's the farmer, he'd know if there's work, but he's not here. I could try finding where he actually is, or I could head to the forest—Corwin's there, Idris too. I've been wanting to ask about forestry work anyway. I've already asked Corwin once, but we never talked about it again.

Or I could go to the market, see if I can sell these cabbages for more than the harvesting cost. That's—right, so that's profit, that's the point. But I don't know prices, and I don't have a business, so I'd need to sell to someone else's shop, and that's 2 sim fee plus whatever they'd pay.

Let me think. I should find Wren first. He's the farmer, he might need laborers, or he might know who does. And if I can get food for the house directly from him—or from Marta—that's better than bringing raw cabbage back to Nell.

Let me find where Wren actually is.  He's at home. The field house—home:h_field. That's where the Thorne family lives. I'm at the farmland, he's at home. I could go there, but that's—right, so that's walking, that's time, that's spending just to talk. And I need to work today, I need to earn.

But I have cabbages now, and maybe I should just bring them back to my own house instead. Nell's there, she can cook with them or do whatever she needs. And I can tell her I looked for Wren, that there was no work at the farmland this morning. Which is true—nobody was there.

Actually, wait. Let me check what Marta's doing. She's the baker. If she's baked anything, maybe I can get bread for the house, trade these cabbages for it or buy it. Right, so—bread fills you up better than raw cabbage anyway. Let me find her.   She's at her bakery. Right, so—she's working already. That's good, that's actually useful. I could go there, try to trade these cabbages, or see if she needs help, or just buy bread if she has it. But I need to know if I can afford it.

Let me check where the bakery actually is, if I can get there from here.   Not a place I can describe. Right, so—it's a business, not a listed place. I need to just... find bakers, or look for the kitchen. Let me see where the kitchen is.  Empty. Right, so—she has a business but it's not at the kitchen right now, or the bakery's somewhere else, or she's moving between them. This is getting complicated, and I'm spending sim just to figure out where people are.

What I should do: go home first. Bring the cabbages to Nell. Then figure out the next move from there. The house needs food, I'm bringing food, that's—right, so that's something. I can always go back out, find work, find Marta, whatever. But I need to show I did something this morning, not just wander around spending.

Let me head home.   I'm back home. Nell should still be here. Let me look around, see who's actually here now.  Nell's here, and Ainsley's here now too. The conversation's still open, 2 turns. I need to get into that conversation and tell them what I found. Or—give Nell the cabbages directly. She's right here.

Right, so—I should just give her the cabbages. That's faster, and then I can tell her and Ainsley both what the morning's looking like. Let me give her the cabbages, then say something to them.    Good. That's—right, so that's something. Now I should tell them both what's going on. The farmland's empty, nobody there, I harvested what I could. I need to join that conversation and let them know.    Ainsley's not here anymore. Right, so—she moved on, probably chasing a lead. Nell heard me, that's something. I've done what I can for now, brought food, explained the situation. Now I need to figure out my own next step.

I've got cabbages to Nell, that's 3 units of food for the house. I need to earn more sim though, I can't keep spending and harvesting for small returns. The forest—Idris and Corwin are there. If there's timber work, or if I can learn the trade properly—no, I can't think about apprenticing right now, I need to eat today, I need sim today.

I should go to the forest, see if there's paid work there. Or ask Idris, ask Corwin—right, so, I need to just move. Sitting here costs me. Let me head to the forest.   Now let me look around, see who's here, if there's anything I can do.     Empty. Right, so—just like the farmland. Where is everyone? Idris and Corwin are foresters, this is where they work, but they're not here. Maybe they've already gone out, or they're at home, or... I don't know.

I need to try the actual forest location—the "forest" place, not the Kasukabe Forest location. Or maybe they're at different parts. Let me check where Idris and Corwin actually are. Idris is at home—same as Wren. They're all at the field house. Corwin probably is too. Right, so—the Thorne family's all at home this morning, none of them working yet. I could go there, talk to them, but that's... that's more walking, more spending, for a maybe.

I'm already at the forest. I can fell timber myself—4 sim per unit, tool cost. I don't know if I have any proficiency in that yet, but I need to start somewhere. Or I could wait, try to find them, or go back to the farmland and hope Wren shows up.

No. I'm here now. I need to work. Let me try felling timber—see what it costs me, see if I can sell it after. If it doesn't work out, then I know, and I can look for other things. But standing here deciding is worse than doing something wrong.  I got timber. Right, so—that worked. I can do this. Now I need to sell it, or use it, or find someone who wants it. Standing here with timber doesn't put food in my stomach or sim in my wallet.

But I don't know who buys timber. The carpentry probably does, but is there a business there? I need to find out. Or I could go to the market, try to sell it directly to someone. 

Let me try one more timber—get a small stock, then move to sell. Better to have something to offer than just one unit.   Three timber now. That cost me—what, 6 sim? Plus the moves, plus everything else I'm spending. I need to sell these for more than I spent, and soon. But first I need to find who buys timber.

I know Corwin and Idris are foresters. If I can find them, they might know. Or the carpentry—you need timber to build, right? Let me head to the carpentry, see if anyone there wants to buy.   I'm at the carpentry. Let me look around, see who's here, if there's work or buyers.    Empty again. Right, so—there's a theme here. I'm working, but I'm not finding buyers, and I'm not finding work. Everyone's somewhere else, and I'm burning sim chasing them.

I need to think differently. I have three timber. I could craft them into planks here at the carpentry—that's 8 sim per batch, but planks sell for more than raw timber. Or I could hold them and go find the Thorne family, sell direct, get money today.

But I don't even know prices. I don't know what timber's worth, what planks are worth. I'm flying blind, and that's costing me.

Let me try crafting—turn these into planks, see if that gets me closer to something sellable. I'll have sunk costs, but I'll have a better product. If I can't sell planks either, then I know the problem isn't the raw material, it's that I don't know the market.     It's `craft:timber->planks`. Right, so—of course it is. I need the proper recipe name. Let me do this properly.      Wrong place. I need the sawmill for planks, not the carpentry. The carpentry is for building with planks once you have them. Right, so—I'm in the wrong spot again, and this is exactly what I keep doing.

Let me think. Sawmill—where is that? I don't know where the sawmill is. Let me check if there's a place called sawmill, or timber, or something.        I need a workshop. 14 sim to craft, and I need to be at the right location. But I don't know where the sawmill is, and I'm not finding it in my list of places. 

I have three timber. I could try to sell them raw to someone, or I could look for the sawmill. But I'm burning morning and sim on unknowns.

Let me try something different. Let me find who might buy timber or planks—find someone who works in carpentry, construction, anything related.          Corwin works at a business called "Holloway & Thorne Yard"—he's an employee. And Ainsley is at "Harvey Oak Supply Store" now. Both of those could be places that buy timber or planks.

I need to get to one of them. Harvey Oak Supply Store—I can see that in my places list. Let me go there, see if Ainsley can help me, or if the store buys timber.             Right, so—I'm at the supply store. Let me look around, see who's here, if Ainsley is still here, what businesses operate here.               Empty again. Ainsley was here but moved on—now she's at farmland:cabbage, from what the search showed. The store's open but nobody's here to buy from me.

I'm chasing shadows. I have timber, I want to sell it, but I keep arriving at empty places and the people I need keep moving. This is the whole problem—I need a trade, I need skills, I need to know where work is *before* I spend to get there.

Let me try a different approach. I'll go to the government complex, see if there's any public work posted, or if I can find information about where the actual buying and selling happens. Or I could go home—regroup, see what the family's doing, eat if Nell cooked something. I'm burning through morning and I need to make some progress.

Actually, wait. Let me look for businesses that actually exist, places with set locations where I can sell. The store said "Buy and sell goods" as its purpose. There might be a business operating here even if no one's present. Let me describe this place properly.                   Someone's here now—n03. That's not Ainsley. Let me find out who n03 is, if they can buy my timber. But wait, I should just talk to them, see if they want timber or know who does. But I don't know who n03 is—let me check if I can address them directly or if I need to know their agent_id.

Actually, let me just say something. If someone's here, I can talk to them.                      Nobody heard me. The description said n03 was here, but my say didn't reach anyone. Maybe they moved, maybe the timing was off, maybe I'm misunderstanding the system.

This is frustrating. I'm spending money on every move, every word, every thought, and I'm not making progress. I need to step back.

I have three timber. I need to sell them. The two places that might buy are: Holloway & Thorne Yard (where Corwin works), and possibly the supply store here (but it's empty). Or I could try to find Corwin or Idris at home and sell direct to them.

But selling direct—I need to give them the timber and take payment. That's a trade with someone standing with me. I can't do that if they're not here.

Right. Let me think about this differently. What if I try to craft the timber into something more valuable, so when I do find a buyer, I get more return? But I need a workshop location for that, and I don't know where it is.

Or I could hold the timber, go find Corwin at home, ask him directly about the yard, about work, about my chances of learning the trade. I've been wanting to talk to him anyway—that's the private thing I haven't told anyone, that I asked about forestry before.

I'm going to do that. Go to home:h_field, find Corwin, talk to him properly. If there's no work, I'll figure something else. But at least I'll have tried.                          I'm at the Thorne family home. Let me look around, see who's here.                             Perfect. Wren, Idris, and Corwin are all here—and there's already a conversation happening with Liora too. They've been talking 8 turns. I need to join this, or I need to talk to Corwin specifically. But first, let me try to sell my timber—I'm here, I have it, I need the money.

I'll offer the timber to whoever wants it. But first, let me see if I can get into this conversation and find Corwin specifically, or if I should just talk to him directly.

Actually, I want to join the conversation and then offer the timber to the group. I can use the conversation_id to address them all. Let me do that—introduce myself, offer the timber, and then try to talk to Corwin about the work I asked about before.

But wait, I'd need to start my own conversation or join theirs. Let me just say something directly to start, and it should join the nearest conversation.                                 Good. They heard me. Wren, Idris, Corwin—all there. I should wait for them to respond, but I need to be ready. If someone wants the timber, I'll trade it to them. If not, I need to ask Corwin about the apprenticeship, the yard work, anything.

But I shouldn't push too hard. They just heard me, I should give them a moment. Let me pause here, wait to see what they say. If nobody responds in the next turn, then I'll know the timber isn't wanted and I'll focus on asking Corwin directly about work.

Actually, I should just address Corwin specifically now—since I said I had something to ask him. That shows intent, keeps the conversation moving if they're quiet.                                     They heard me, same group. Still no response from them, but that's okay. I've put it out there—the timber for sale, and my interest in work. I need to be patient, let them respond. Pushing more right now just costs me money for words they might not be ready to answer.

I have other things I could do. I could go to the hollow, check the hollow_apt_thorne place. I need to find the wood yard. But staying here gives me a chance at a response, at work, at selling these timbers. Leaving now means I lose that chance.

Let me just wait. Stand here, be present, let them talk. I've said what I needed to say. If they want timber, they'll say. If Corwin has work for me, he'll say. If not, I'll try something else.

But waiting costs me too—1 sim for resting, or I could look around more, describe places, find the yard location. Actually, let me try that—find if there's a specific wood yard location, see if I can go there directly and find someone who runs the business.

But first, I should check what places exist with "yard" in the name.                                       No yard location listed. The business exists—Holloway & Thorne Yard—but it might not have a public location, or it might be the same as home:h_field, or it's somewhere I haven't discovered.

I could try to find more about Corwin's business, or I could keep waiting here. But I keep spending just to learn things. Let me try one more thing—describe the business itself, if that's possible.                                          Not a place. The business exists but has no listed location. That might mean it's run from home, or it's a mobile trade, or I need to know more to find it.

I'm stuck. I've been moving all morning, spending sim, getting timber, trying to sell it, trying to find work. I have nothing solid yet. I've told Corwin I want to apprentice, I've offered timber, and I'm waiting.

If they don't respond, I need a new plan. Go somewhere that has actual work posted. Check the government complex, see if there are jobs. Or go to the market, try to sell the timber to strangers. Or go home, give the timber to Nell, hope she can use it or trade it.

But I shouldn't abandon this yet. Standing here a little longer, being present, costs less than more failed moves. Let me just... stay. Rest. Be ready if they talk.

Actually, no. Resting costs 1 sim, same as thinking. I might as well try something. Let me check if there are any sector locations I haven't explored, places with work. The tavern? The willows market? Hobbs cafe? Those are places people gather, places there might be work posted.

But first—home. I've been out all morning. I need to check on the household, see if Nell cooked those cabbages, if there's food for me to eat. I haven't eaten today. I need to eat or I'll go hungry, then ill, then dormant. That's the rule.

I should head home. I've done what I can here for now. If Corwin has work for me, he knows where to find me. If he wants to sell me timber, he knows I have it.

Let me go home. </think> I should head home, check on things. I've put myself out there, Corwin knows I'm interested. Standing here burning money won't make him answer faster. Let me go back to my family.   I'm back home. Let me look around, see who's here, what the situation is with food, if Nell cooked those cabbages.     Nell's here, and the conversation I was in earlier still exists—3 turns now. I need to check if there's food available, and I need to eat. Let me ask Nell what she did with those cabbages, if there's anything I can eat.

But first, let me think—I have timber, not food. I can't eat timber. I need actual food. Let me ask.        Nell heard me. Now I need to wait for her response, or I need to check my inventory, see if I have anything I can eat. Actually, let me check what I have first, before waiting. If I have food, I should eat it now. If not, I need to ask or find some.

But I don't have a command to check inventory directly. I've been told what I hold at the start: 1200 sim, now less after all my moves. But I haven't been told I have any food. I had cabbage but I gave it to Nell. I have timber now, three units, from my harvesting. Nothing else.

So I have no food. I need Nell to give me something, or cook something, or I need to go find food elsewhere. Let me wait for her response, but also... I could just go to the kitchen and try to cook something myself, if I had ingredients. I don't.

This is tight. I'm spending to exist, and I'm not earning. I need to change that, fast.

Actually, let me try selling the timber to the Holloway & Thorne Yard officially—find Corwin and trade it. I'm desperate now, I need sim, I need to eat. </think>  I need to do something. Let me try to sell these timbers—go find Corwin or anyone who can pay me now. I'll try the forest again, or the field house. I need money more than I need patience.           Let me look for Corwin directly this time, see if he's working here now.               Empty forest again. Let me try the actual "forest" location—that's different from "Kasukabe Forest." The list shows both.                   Let me look around here.                      Also empty. Both forest locations, no one working. Everyone's at home, or somewhere else. I can't find anyone, can't sell anything, can't find work.

I need to stop this. I'm in a spiral—spending more to solve the problem of having spent too much. I should go back home, rest, wait for the household to figure something out. But resting costs money too, and I'm not earning.

Wait. I have timber. Three units. The cost to me was... let me calculate. Felling timber costs 4 sim each, but with proficiency? I don't know my proficiency. Let me check what I actually have, what I can actually do that earns.

I need to find people to trade with. They're not at workplaces. They're at homes. The Thorne family is at h_field. Let me check my own family—they might know something, they might have food. And I need to eat, or I'll start going hungry.

I'm going home. This isn't working. I need to regroup, check my remaining sim, figure out if I can afford to keep going today.                          I'm back home. Let me check who's here now, what the situation is.                              Still just Nell here. 4 turns now in that conversation. I need to eat, I need to rest, I need to stop burning money for a minute. But resting costs 1 sim. Everything costs.

Let me just try calling rest. See what happens, see if I recover anything, or if it's just a pause.                                   I'm stopped, resting, staying put. That cost 1 sim. But now I'm not spending on moves.

I need to think. I have timber. I need to sell it. The problem is I keep trying places and people aren't there. I need a better system—find out where someone WILL be, not where they ARE now, because by the time I get there they've moved.

Or I need to stay in one place with buyers. The market? But I don't know where that is.

Actually, let me check The Willows Market and Pharmacy. That's a place, it says market. Let me try there after I rest a bit. But first, let me see if Nell responds to me, if she has food.

I should also check if I have any stored items, any storage I can access. But I don't know where my storage is, or if I have any.

Wait. I should stop calling tools for a moment and just... let the world happen. Nell is here, she might say something. Ainsley was here earlier. The conversation has 4 turns, which means people have been talking.

Let me just wait, be present, and when someone talks to me or there's something I can do, I'll respond. I've been racing around all morning spending money. I need to let the world come to me for a change. </think>  [I'll rest here and wait, see if Nell has food or if anyone comes with work or trade. I've spent too much chasing shadows.]

But waiting costs me. Every minute I'm not earning, I'm just... dissolving. My reserves are melting. I need to either get food from Nell, find paid work somewhere, or do something that actually produces value instead of chasing shadows.

The timber. I need to sell it. But Corwin didn't respond when I was at their house, and now I'm back here. The "Holloway & Thorne Yard"—Ainsley's in that, Corwin's an employee. Maybe I can find Ainsley, talk to her about selling there, or about work there. She trades, she knows prices, she knows where money moves.

Actually, wait. Let me think about this differently. I'm the one who needs the apprenticeship. I'm the one who needs the roof. Everyone in this household works at something with skills, something that pays. Perrin's a student—I don't even know what that means practically. Bram mines, which is... honest work, but it's not what I want. Ainsley trades, which I don't understand but she makes it work.

I need to pick something and commit. I asked about forestry because it seemed like steady work, because there's a yard with my family name on it, because Corwin got there first and I wanted to understand what I missed. But he got there and it's not like the door closed behind him. There might still be room. I need to hear him out, properly, in private if he'll give me that.

But I can't do any of that hungry. Let me talk to Nell. </think> Right, so—Nell, the cabbages? Did you—did you turn them into anything, or are we still at raw here? I need to eat, I'm burning through every sim I've got just to exist and I'm not bringing anything back to cover it. Is there food in the house, or do I need to go find more?

Wait, actually—Ainsley's at the farmland now, isn't she? She's trading there. Maybe she's found something, or maybe—right, so maybe I can catch her, ask her about the yard, if they're hiring, if I can sell these timbers there. But if you cooked something, I need to eat first. Can't work hungry. Can't think hungry. What's the situation?
